name: Money Mules
description: Individuals, witting or unwitting, whose accounts or identities are used to receive and move criminal proceeds on behalf of others, often recruited via fake job offers, romance scams or social media. Mule activity is a key layering and cash-out step for fraud and other crime proceeds.

sources.text: Europol, EU Money Mule Action (EMMA) campaign press releases
FATF, Money Laundering from Fraud typology guidance (general)
FinCEN, advisories on money mule activity (general)

exposure.rationale: Mule accounts receive and forward funds rapidly, often young or new customers.

indicators.name: Inbound third-party payments followed by rapid outbound transfers
indicators.desc: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.
indicators.ctx: Account receives credits from unrelated payers and sends most funds onward within hours or days, retaining a small amount.
indicators.fp: Marketplace sellers, agents and family support flows may pass funds on quickly.

indicators.name: New or recently opened account with sudden high activity
indicators.canon: New account or entity with sudden high activity
indicators.desc: A recently opened account or newly formed entity with little history abruptly sees large or numerous payments unrelated to its profile.
indicators.ctx: Account shows little history then abruptly receives many payments unrelated to the profile.
indicators.fp: Students or new arrivals may receive lump sums such as loans or grants.

indicators.name: Account holder profile matches common recruitment demographics
indicators.canon: Account activity inconsistent with declared occupation or income
indicators.desc: Turnover or volumes materially exceed what the customer's declared occupation, income, age or circumstances would support.
indicators.ctx: Young, unemployed or newly arrived customers with high flows inconsistent with their stated circumstances.
indicators.fp: Profile alone is not suspicious and must not drive discrimination.

indicators.name: Customer follows instructions or is coached
indicators.canon: Customer accompanied, directed or coached by a third party
indicators.desc: Another person speaks for, accompanies or dictates instructions to the customer, who may appear fearful, scripted or unable to explain the activity.
indicators.ctx: In branch or in contact, the customer cannot explain transactions, reads from scripts, or is accompanied by a handler.
indicators.fp: Vulnerable or elderly customers may need help for genuine reasons.

indicators.name: Shared devices, IP addresses or contact details across accounts
indicators.canon: Shared devices, IP addresses or contact details across accounts
indicators.desc: Multiple unrelated accounts share devices, phone numbers, email or addresses.
indicators.ctx: Multiple unrelated accounts share devices, phone numbers, email or addresses.
indicators.fp: Households and shared workplaces share details.

indicators.name: Payments carrying scam-related references
indicators.desc: Payment narratives or references contain wording linked to scams such as safe accounts or investment schemes.
indicators.ctx: Inbound payments with references typical of fraud, e.g. invoice, loan fee, investment or romance context.

indicators.name: Account credentials accessed from remote locations or by third parties
indicators.canon: Account credentials accessed from remote locations or by third parties
indicators.desc: Logins from foreign IPs or remote-access tools soon after opening.
indicators.ctx: Logins from foreign IPs or remote-access tools soon after opening.
indicators.fp: Travel and VPN use are common.

indicators.name: International transfers or cryptocurrency purchases following credits
indicators.canon: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt
indicators.desc: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.
indicators.ctx: Funds exit via overseas transfers, gift cards or crypto purchases after receipt.
indicators.fp: International students and migrants send money abroad.

indicators.name: Multiple accounts opened for same individual or by same agent
indicators.canon: One person holding multiple identities or accounts
indicators.desc: The same individual appears under different names or opens several accounts or wallets, directly or through an intermediary.
indicators.ctx: One person or intermediary opens accounts at several institutions or products.
